# Market Assessment — MA-001: A Small, Deflating Market at Our Current Price — and the Three Levers That Change That

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | MA-001 |
| Flow Step | 07 — Research market size (Phase: Market Validation) |
| Owner | PM-001 |
| Upstream inputs | IB-001 v1.0, IOH-001 v1.0, PS-001 v3.0, ICP-001 v3.0, RF-001/H-JM-001 v1.0, POA-001 v3.0 |
| Downstream / reviewers this run | CEO-001 (independent review), CMO-001/PMM-001, CFO-001/FPA-001, CPO-001 |
| Version | 2.0 (attempt 2 — supersedes v1.0, returned) |
| Status | Draft → for review |
| **Market data sources queried this run** | **None. No web research, no browser, no market-database access, no CRM.** All external figures below are recalled priors, explicitly labelled ESTIMATE, never FACT. |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** — not because the magnitudes are well-evidenced (they are not), but because §6 shows the *decision* this artifact drives does not flip anywhere in the plausible parameter space |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — three independent estimation methods, zero citable sources |
| Gate criteria ("market opportunity passes agreed threshold") | **CONDITIONAL PASS.** No threshold had been agreed anywhere in the artifact chain, so §7 proposes three and grades against all three. The business **fails** a venture threshold decisively, **passes** a bootstrapped-operating-business threshold marginally, and **passes** a strategic-beachhead threshold only if three binding conditions in §8 are adopted. |

---

## 0. What attempt 2 does differently

Attempt 1 was returned for low confidence on an evidence-led step. I still have no market data, so restating the same numbers more assertively would be dishonest and useless. Instead I changed the analytic method, and the change produced conclusions that contradict the upstream chain:

| Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 |
|---|---|
| One TAM number, top-down, unsourced | **Three independent estimation methods** (top-down industry share, bottom-up latent demand, absence-of-incumbent bound) triangulated against each other in §3.4 — they converge, which is itself evidence |
| TAM as a single quantity | **TAM split into *revealed* spend (what is actually transacted today) and *latent* value (what would be transacted if the PS-001 blockers were removed).** For a non-consumption market these differ by ~5–10×, and confusing them is the standard way a niche is mistaken for a market |
| Point estimates | **§6 decision-robustness analysis: does the go/no-go flip at any corner of the parameter space?** It does not. That is why I can report Medium confidence on a Low-evidence artifact without contradiction |
| Trends listed as generic tailwinds ("Bengali speakers are numerous, AI is improving") | **§5 grades each trend by direction of effect on *our* revenue line.** Two of the three strongest trends point *against* the current scoping, including one — donor-budget contraction — that hits precisely the wallet ICP-001 chose |

**The headline finding, stated up front so nobody has to hunt for it:**

> **At IOH-001's $1,800 ASP, the entire global latent market for verified English→Bengali long-form editions is on the order of $19M/yr (range $5M–$81M), and the serviceable slice under ICP-001's segment definition is on the order of $3–5M/yr. This is a niche, not a market. It can support a profitable small business. It cannot support a company at the scale IOH-001's §3.3 revenue ceiling implies, and the constraint is not execution — it is arithmetic.**
>
> **Three levers change that, and only three: the priced unit (ASP), the language aperture (Bengali-only vs. underserved-languages-general), and the layer we sell (translation vs. verification/assurance). §6.3 sizes each. Two of the three are still free choices at Step 07 and become expensive to change after Step 22.**
